summary: Rule-clean, well-scoped port of the proven bf16_proj split-K hi/lo router, but the premise that the router branch is on the turn_1 critical path rests on misidentifying the pooler as the 39 us nvjet; the pooler is in the 128x192 group (~55-70 us), so the side branch most likely already fits under it and the realistic headline effect is SM-contention relief of ~0.3-1%, inside the +/-1.5% interval. Run it for the router kernel's own time (readable from top_kernels), not for the headline, and given 2 checks left it should not displace the in-flight rewrite's next stage.
justification: Mechanism: a 3-D split-K Triton GEMM with fp32 atomic_add into a zeroed output and hi+lo dots on the same x tile is sound on H200 and was the one large bf16 win (1.151x in muse_bf16_proj, LESSONS). On cuBLAS's own time the case is plausible: at M=753 the pair runs as nvjet_tss_64x96 splitK (33.2 us sliding / 39.6 us full, 2 calls) for 6.3 GFLOP (~160-190 TFLOP/s), and at M=3012 as nvjet_tss_64x104 (132.4 / 134.9 us, 2 calls) for 25.3 GFLOP (~190 TFLOP/s), so a Triton kernel at 300-450 TFLOP/s would cut the router to ~15-25 us and ~55-85 us respectively. The critical-path argument is the weak part. (1) The pooler is not the 39 us kernel: nvjet_112x128 is a single call and 50.5 GFLOP (753x4096x8192x2) in 39.3 us would be 1.28 PFLOP/s, above the 989 TFLOP/s peak; it is the qkv_gate GEMM (N=2304, 28.4 GFLOP, ~720 TFLOP/s). The pooler is one of the three nvjet_128x192 calls (o, pooler, unpooler: 113.6 GFLOP in 157-162 us), i.e. ~60-70 us while sharing SMs with the router, plus the 6.6 us pre-expert norm: a main branch of ~65-80 us. (2) The side branch on turn_1 sliding is 33.2 us of router GEMM plus a splitKreduce and FusedMuseSparkRouting that are both below the 5.1 us top-12 cut-off: ~40-45 us. So the side branch is very likely already shorter than the main branch, which is the opposite of the moe-align-side-stream review's premise that this hypothesis inherits. (3) The 45.6 us splitKreduce on turn_1 full (absent from the sliding top-12 for identical M and identical router code) is almost certainly wait time folded into an overlapping kernel's row (the profile says so explicitly), not real reduce work; it cannot be used as the size of the prize. What remains is contention: both branches are wave-filling (pooler 128x192 tiles: 6x22=132 CTAs at M=753; the Triton config is 192 CTAs at ~144 KB smem, 1 CTA/SM, two partial waves), so the headline moves only by the SM-time the router stops stealing from the pooler, roughly the difference in router SM-time: ~10-20 us at turn_1 (~1% of 1079/1435 us) and ~50-80 us at turn_4 (~1-1.5% of 3367/4950 us). Note turn_4 may actually be the better load, not turn_1, contrary to the expected block. first_turn flat is right (cuBLAS kept above 4096). Directions are consistent with TASK.md weights (turn_1 and turn_4 sliding carry w46 each, so a ~1% per-shape move is ~0.3-0.5% on the geomean after the first_turn load's flat 1/3), but magnitudes land inside the interval. Second weak link: the config (128x128x64, 8 warps, 3 stages, SPLIT_K 16/4) is not the measured one (bf16_proj ran 64x64x128 at m<=256, ~128 CTAs). At SPLIT_K 16 each CTA has only 8 BLOCK_K steps of a 3-stage pipeline, so prologue/epilogue and 16 x 753 x 256 fp32 atomics (~12 MB of L2 atomic traffic) are a real fraction of the work; the 'ported, proven' claim covers the kernel skeleton, not this operating point. Weakest link overall: the pooler misidentification, which turns 'removes ~40 us from the critical path' into 'reduces SM contention by ~10-20 us'.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: it is the base (the whole file against the plain-PyTorch starter), not a separable confounder. Its side-stream fork placing the router beside the pooler is exactly what decides whether a faster router shows in the headline (critical path vs contention). The change would behave the same with any base that keeps the fork; reverting the patch removes the fork, Marlin and the router path together, so there is nothing to A/B against.
interference: No companion is warranted. ab-revert has no target: the only landed hypothesis is the parity base, and reversing muse_prefill_layer/hypotheses/done/gain/sglang-pipeline-parity.patch returns to the starter with no side stream. ab-tune has no meaningful knob on the landed side (moving the router to the main stream is the sibling router-pooler-concat-gemm-turn's territory and would change the comparison point). A control is also not needed because the result is attributable without one: the replaced kernel's own time is directly readable in top_kernels (the two nvjet_tss splitK rows and the splitKreduce disappear and one _router_hilo_kernel row appears; Triton times reproduce within ~1%), and the 4096-token gate leaves first_turn as a built-in control. A per-shape gain on turn_1/turn_4 with a faster router row is the change; a loss with a faster router row is contention of a 192-CTA, 1-CTA/SM Triton kernel against the pooler (read the pooler's 128x192 row for inflation); a loss with a slower router row is the untested config. With 2 checks left today, spending a second on a companion that can only resolve sub-1% effects is not justified.
rules_flags: None that break a rule. The hi+lo BF16 split with FP32 accumulation is explicitly permitted for the router (TASK.md Weights); keeping a second untransposed copy of hi/lo is a lossless repack in prepare().
Branching on tokens (<= 4096, <= 1024) is a shape branch, allowed. Config is chosen from tokens only, so nothing depends on input values.

torch.zeros inside the side-stream block becomes a memset node in the captured graph; that is an allocation from the graph pool, not a host sync, and it already happens for other per-call buffers. It must be issued on the side stream (inside the with-block), not before the fork, or the main-stream memset adds to the critical path and the side stream needs it ordered.

Pre-compiling both buckets in prepare() on synthetic BF16 x is required: a JIT compile inside the timed/captured call would fail capture or be charged; also pre-compile for the test shapes' M range (600, 1506, 3012, 4096 tokens all fall in the two buckets, so do_not_specialize M covers them).

Atomic fp32 accumulation order is nondeterministic; this changes logits by fp32 ulps only and the routing near-tie tolerance (0.05 of the 8th best, 0.03/0.04 margin) absorbs it, as on bf16_proj. The 'outliers' dist test (batch 3, q_len 200) is the one most likely to surface a near tie; it is not a rule issue.

Triton launches use torch.cuda.current_stream(), so launching inside the existing torch.cuda.stream(side_stream) block keeps the fork/join; confirm record_stream on the eager path also covers the new logits buffer (it is consumed only on the side stream, so it does today implicitly).
open_questions: Which nvjet_128x192 call is the pooler and how long is it while the router runs beside it? A per-call breakdown (or the profile's json) would settle whether the side branch is on the turn_1 critical path at all; if it is not, the expected block's turn_1 'up to ~40 us' should be read as at most ~10-20 us.
Is the 45.6 us splitKreduce on turn_1 full real work or wait time? It is absent from turn_1 sliding's top 12 for identical M and identical router code, which points to wait.

Is 128x128x64 / 8 warps / 3 stages with SPLIT_K 16 (8 K-steps per CTA) better than the measured bf16_proj shape scaled up (64x64x128 or 64x128x128, ~128-192 CTAs)? Only the router row's own time answers it; if the row is not under ~25 us at M=753, the config, not the idea, is the problem.

Should this run before router-pooler-concat-gemm-turn? They target the same branch and do not stack; this one is the cheaper, lower-risk read of whether the router branch matters at all, and its router-row time sizes the concat's best case. Given prefill's 2 remaining checks today and the in-flight swapab rewrite, consider deferring both router hypotheses to tomorrow's quota unless the rewrite's stage 2 is not ready.
